meaning: Speak angrily to someone because you disagree with them.
japanese: 人と言い争う。口論する。
cue: Two children are shouting about whose turn it is.
reply: Please don't argue with your sister about the game.
replyJapanese: ゲームのことで、お姉ちゃんと言い合いをしないでね。
transferCue: Explain why you were late leaving the house.
transferReply: I argued with my dad about money this morning.
transferReplyJapanese: 今朝、お金のことで父と口論になりました。
nuance: Use with for the person and about for the topic. Do not say argue to someone.
nuanceJapanese: 相手は with、話題は about で示す。argue to someone とは言わない。
contrast: Argue with is an angry fight in words; disagree with can be calm and polite.
contrastJapanese: argue with は言葉での怒ったけんか。disagree with は穏やかで丁寧な場合もある。

meaning: Ask for news of someone, for example how they are.
japanese: 人の様子や近況を尋ねる。
cue: You met your sister's old teacher in town.
reply: Mrs Hill asked about you in the shop today.
replyJapanese: 今日お店で、ヒルさんがあなたの様子を尋ねていたよ。
transferCue: A colleague has been off sick for two weeks.
transferReply: Everyone at work keeps asking about you.
transferReplyJapanese: 職場のみんなが、あなたはどうしているかと何度も尋ねています。
nuance: The person follows about, and the question is usually about their health or news. Ask after someone means the same and is more British.
nuanceJapanese: about のあとに人を置き、たいてい体調や近況を尋ねる。ask after someone も同じ意味で、よりイギリス的。
contrast: Ask about wants news of a person; ask for wants to speak to them or to get something.
contrastJapanese: ask about は人の近況を知りたいとき。ask for はその人と話したい、または何かが欲しいとき。

meaning: Cut something into small pieces.
japanese: 小さく切り分ける。
cue: A small child cannot eat a large piece of chicken.
reply: I'll cut up the chicken for you.
replyJapanese: 鶏肉を小さく切ってあげるね。
transferCue: Explain how to make a fruit salad.
transferReply: Cut the apples up and put them in a bowl.
transferReplyJapanese: りんごを小さく切って、ボウルに入れます。
nuance: Separable: cut up the meat or cut the meat up. A pronoun goes in the middle: cut it up.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：cut up the meat でも cut the meat up でもよい。代名詞は間に置く：cut it up。
contrast: Cut up makes many small pieces; cut off removes one part from the rest.
contrastJapanese: cut up はいくつもの小片にする。cut off は一部を切り離す。

meaning: Trust someone or something to help you or do what you need.
japanese: 頼りにする。当てにする。
cue: Promise a friend that you will help on moving day.
reply: You can depend on me this Saturday.
replyJapanese: 今度の土曜日は、私を頼りにしていいよ。
transferCue: Explain why you drive to work in winter.
transferReply: We can't depend on the buses when it snows.
transferReplyJapanese: 雪が降ると、バスは当てにできません。
nuance: The preposition is on, not to or of. Upon is a formal choice. It depends on also means be decided by: It depends on the weather.
nuanceJapanese: 前置詞は on で、to や of は使わない。upon は改まった形。It depends on the weather のように「〜次第だ」の意味にもなる。
contrast: Depend on and rely on are very close; count on is more casual and friendly.
contrastJapanese: depend on と rely on はほぼ同じ。count on はもっとくだけた、親しみのある言い方。

meaning: Have a meal at home, not in a restaurant.
japanese: 外食せずに、家で食事をする。
cue: You are too tired to go to a restaurant.
reply: Let's eat in tonight and watch a film.
replyJapanese: 今夜は家で食べて、映画を見よう。
transferCue: Say how you saved money last month.
transferReply: We ate in every night to save money.
transferReplyJapanese: 節約のために、毎晩家で食事をしました。
nuance: No object follows. In a café, eat in can also mean having your food there, not taking it away.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は取らない。カフェでは「持ち帰らずに店内で食べる」の意味にもなる。
contrast: Eat in means a meal at home; eat out means a meal in a restaurant.
contrastJapanese: eat in は家での食事。eat out はレストランでの食事。

meaning: Stop thinking about something or someone.
japanese: もう考えないようにする。忘れる。
cue: A friend is still upset about a small mistake at work.
reply: Just forget about it and enjoy your weekend.
replyJapanese: そのことはもう忘れて、週末を楽しんで。
transferCue: Describe a relaxing holiday.
transferReply: On the beach I forgot about work completely.
transferReplyJapanese: ビーチでは、仕事のことをすっかり忘れていました。
nuance: Forget about it is a kind way to say something does not matter. After about, use a noun or an -ing form.
nuanceJapanese: Forget about it は「気にしないで」というやさしい言い方。about のあとは名詞か -ing 形。
contrast: Forget about means stop thinking of it; forget alone means fail to remember a fact or leave a thing behind.
contrastJapanese: forget about は考えるのをやめること。forget だけなら、事実を思い出せない、または物を置き忘れること。

meaning: Enter a room or building.
japanese: 中に入る。
cue: You and a friend are standing outside a café in the cold.
reply: It's freezing out here, so let's go in.
replyJapanese: ここは凍えそうに寒いから、中に入ろう。
transferCue: Explain a rule to a guest at your front door.
transferReply: Please take your shoes off before you go in.
transferReplyJapanese: 中に入る前に、靴を脱いでください。
nuance: No object follows go in. To name the place, use into: go into the shop.
nuanceJapanese: go in のあとに目的語は置かない。場所を言うときは into を使う：go into the shop。
contrast: Go in is said from outside the place; come in is said by someone who is already inside.
contrastJapanese: go in は外にいる側から言う。come in はすでに中にいる人が言う。

meaning: Want something good to happen.
japanese: そうなってほしいと願う。期待する。
cue: You are planning a picnic in the park.
reply: We're hoping for a sunny day on Sunday.
replyJapanese: 日曜日は晴れてほしいと思っています。
transferCue: A family is waiting at the hospital.
transferReply: We can only wait and hope for good news.
transferReplyJapanese: あとは待って、いい知らせを願うことしかできません。
nuance: A noun follows for. Before a verb, use hope to; before a clause, use hope that: I hope that it stops raining.
nuanceJapanese: for のあとは名詞。動詞の前では hope to、文の前では hope that を使う：I hope that it stops raining。
contrast: Hope for is used when something may really happen; wish for is for things that are unlikely.
contrastJapanese: hope for は実際に起こりそうなことに使う。wish for は起こりそうにないことに使う。

meaning: Get new knowledge about a subject.
japanese: あることについて学ぶ。知識を得る。
cue: Explain what happens on a new employee's first day.
reply: New staff learn about the company on their first day.
replyJapanese: 新入社員は、初日に会社について学びます。
transferCue: A child comes home and talks about school.
transferReply: We learned about volcanoes in science today.
transferReplyJapanese: 今日は理科で火山について習ったよ。
nuance: Use about for a topic: learn about space. For a skill or a language, use no preposition: learn English, learn to swim.
nuanceJapanese: 話題には about を使う：learn about space。技能や言語には前置詞を付けない：learn English、learn to swim。
contrast: Learn about means study a topic over time; hear about means someone tells you a piece of news.
contrastJapanese: learn about は時間をかけて題材を学ぶこと。hear about は人から知らせを聞くこと。

meaning: Start to live in a new home.
japanese: 新しい住まいに引っ越す。入居する。
cue: Tell a friend when your new home will be ready.
reply: We're moving into the new flat next month.
replyJapanese: 来月、新しいアパートに引っ越します。
transferCue: Describe your new neighbours.
transferReply: A young couple moved into the house next door.
transferReplyJapanese: 若い夫婦が、隣の家に引っ越してきました。
nuance: A place must follow into: move into a flat. With no place, say move in: We moved in last week.
nuanceJapanese: into のあとには必ず場所を置く：move into a flat。場所を言わないときは move in：We moved in last week。
contrast: Move into starts life in a new home; move out of leaves the old one.
contrastJapanese: move into は新しい家に住み始める。move out of は前の家を出る。

meaning: Order ready food to be brought to your home or office.
japanese: 出前を頼む。料理を配達してもらう。
cue: The team is staying late at the office to finish a job.
reply: Nobody has time to go out, so let's order in.
replyJapanese: 誰も外に出る時間がないので、出前を頼みましょう。
transferCue: Tell a friend about your quiet Friday evening.
transferReply: It was raining, so we ordered in a curry.
transferReplyJapanese: 雨が降っていたので、カレーの出前を頼みました。
nuance: Mainly American; British speakers more often say get a takeaway. It can be used with or without the food as an object.
nuanceJapanese: 主にアメリカ英語。イギリスでは get a takeaway と言うことが多い。料理を目的語にしても、しなくても使える。
contrast: Order in means the food is cooked elsewhere and delivered; eat in can also be food you cook yourself.
contrastJapanese: order in は外で作った料理を届けてもらうこと。eat in は自分で作った食事でもよい。

meaning: Put something into a box or bag, or back where it is kept.
japanese: 箱や袋に入れてしまう。片づける。
cue: The camping trip is over and rain is coming.
reply: Let's pack away the tent before it rains.
replyJapanese: 雨が降る前に、テントをしまおう。
transferCue: Describe a job you did when spring came.
transferReply: I packed my winter clothes away in a big box.
transferReplyJapanese: 冬服を大きな箱にしまいました。
nuance: Separable: pack away the tent or pack the tent away. A pronoun goes in the middle: pack it away.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：pack away the tent でも pack the tent away でもよい。代名詞は間に置く：pack it away。
contrast: Pack away stores things in a box or bag for later; tidy away just puts them back in their usual places.
contrastJapanese: pack away は箱や袋に入れて保管する。tidy away はいつもの場所に戻すだけ。

meaning: Go past a person or place without stopping.
japanese: そばを通り過ぎる。
cue: Describe a slow afternoon by the river.
reply: I sat outside and watched the boats pass by.
replyJapanese: 外に座って、船が通り過ぎるのを眺めていました。
transferCue: Offer to post a letter for a colleague.
transferReply: I pass by the post office on my way home.
transferReplyJapanese: 帰り道に郵便局の前を通りますよ。
nuance: It means going past without stopping. A place can follow: pass by the station. A passer-by is a person who is walking past.
nuanceJapanese: 立ち止まらずに通り過ぎること。pass by the station のように場所を続けられる。passer-by は通りすがりの人。
contrast: Pass by goes past without stopping; drop by means stopping for a short visit.
contrastJapanese: pass by は立ち寄らずに通り過ぎる。drop by は少し立ち寄ること。

meaning: Expect something to happen and get ready for it.
japanese: これから起こることに備える。準備する。
cue: Heavy snow is coming and the roads will be slow.
reply: We should prepare for long delays tomorrow.
replyJapanese: 明日は、大幅な遅れに備えておいたほうがいいです。
transferCue: Say why your sister cannot come out tonight.
transferReply: She's preparing for her driving test next week.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は来週の運転免許の試験に向けて準備しています。
nuance: Prepare for a test means get ready to take it; prepare a test means write the questions. Prepare yourself for is common before bad news.
nuanceJapanese: prepare for a test は受ける準備をすること。prepare a test は問題を作ること。悪い知らせの前では prepare yourself for をよく使う。
contrast: Prepare for is a little formal; get ready for is the everyday way to say the same thing.
contrastJapanese: prepare for はやや改まった言い方。get ready for は同じ意味の日常的な言い方。

meaning: Phone someone again, or phone someone who called you earlier.
japanese: 電話をかけ直す。折り返し電話する。
cue: A customer phones while you are in a meeting.
reply: Can I ring you back in ten minutes?
replyJapanese: 10分後にかけ直してもよろしいですか。
transferCue: Give a colleague a message after lunch.
transferReply: The bank rang back while you were at lunch.
transferReplyJapanese: お昼に出ている間に、銀行から折り返しの電話がありました。
nuance: British English; Americans say call back. A pronoun goes in the middle: ring me back, not ring back me.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカでは call back と言う。代名詞は間に置く：ring me back。ring back me とは言わない。
contrast: Ring back returns or repeats a call; ring up simply makes a call.
contrastJapanese: ring back は折り返す、またはかけ直すこと。ring up は単に電話をかけること。

meaning: Make a phone call to someone.
japanese: 電話をかける。
cue: You and a friend want to eat out on Saturday.
reply: I'll ring up the restaurant and book a table.
replyJapanese: レストランに電話して、席を予約しておきます。
transferCue: Tell a friend about a surprise call last night.
transferReply: My cousin rang me up last night for a chat.
transferReplyJapanese: ゆうべ、いとこがおしゃべりしたくて電話をかけてきました。
nuance: British and informal; Americans say call up. A pronoun goes in the middle: ring her up. In a shop, ring up also means enter a price on the till.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語のくだけた言い方で、アメリカでは call up。代名詞は間に置く：ring her up。店ではレジに金額を打ち込む意味にもなる。
contrast: Ring up starts a phone call; hang up ends one.
contrastJapanese: ring up は電話をかけること。hang up は電話を切ること。

meaning: Fold something around itself to make a tube or ball.
japanese: くるくると巻く。丸める。
cue: The yoga class has just finished.
reply: We rolled up our mats and went home.
replyJapanese: マットを巻いて、家に帰りました。
transferCue: Tell a friend how to carry a large poster.
transferReply: Roll the poster up and put it in this tube.
transferReplyJapanese: ポスターを丸めて、この筒に入れてください。
nuance: Separable: roll up the map or roll it up. With sleeves or trousers it means folding them to make them shorter.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：roll up the map でも roll it up でもよい。袖やズボンの場合は、折り返して短くすること。
contrast: Roll up turns something into a tube or ball; fold up makes it flat and smaller.
contrastJapanese: roll up は筒や玉の形に巻く。fold up は平らに小さくたたむ。

meaning: Look carefully in a place to find someone who is missing.
japanese: 行方のわからない人を、念入りに捜す。
cue: Your little boy walked away in a big department store.
reply: We searched for our son on every floor.
replyJapanese: すべての階で息子を捜し回りました。
transferCue: Read out a news story about a walker lost in the hills.
transferReply: Police are still searching for the missing walker.
transferReplyJapanese: 警察は、行方不明のハイカーの捜索を今も続けています。
nuance: For comes before the person you want to find; the place comes straight after search: search the park for a child. It is also used for lost things.
nuanceJapanese: for のあとに捜す相手を置き、場所は search の直後に置く：search the park for a child。なくした物を探すときにも使う。
contrast: Search for is a careful, serious hunt; look for is the everyday choice for small things.
contrastJapanese: search for は念入りで本格的な捜索。look for はちょっとした物を探すときの日常的な言い方。

meaning: Send the same thing to a lot of people.
japanese: 大勢の人に送る。発送する。
cue: The office will close early on Friday and staff need to know.
reply: I'll send out an email to everyone today.
replyJapanese: 今日、全員にメールを送ります。
transferCue: Say when you told guests about your wedding.
transferReply: We sent the invitations out in March.
transferReplyJapanese: 招待状は3月に発送しました。
nuance: Use it when one thing goes to many people. Separable: send out the letters or send them out.
nuanceJapanese: 同じものを多くの人に送るときに使う。分離できる：send out the letters でも send them out でもよい。
contrast: Send out goes to many people at once; send off posts one letter or parcel.
contrastJapanese: send out は一度に多くの人へ送る。send off は手紙や小包をひとつ発送する。

meaning: Stop talking or making a noise.
japanese: 黙る。静かにする。
cue: Your brother talked all through a film you wanted to watch.
reply: He never shut up during the film.
replyJapanese: 彼は映画のあいだ、一度も黙らなかったんだ。
transferCue: Explain why two classmates stopped speaking to each other.
transferReply: She told him to shut up and he got angry.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女が「黙って」と言ったので、彼は怒ってしまいました。
nuance: Rude when said straight to someone, so understand it but use it with care. Please be quiet is the polite choice.
nuanceJapanese: 相手に直接言うと失礼なので、意味は知っておき、使うときは注意する。丁寧に言うなら Please be quiet。
contrast: Shut up is strong and rude; quieten down is a gentler way to ask for less noise.
contrastJapanese: shut up は強くて失礼な言い方。quieten down は静かにするよう穏やかに求める言い方。

meaning: Sing together with music that someone else is singing or playing.
japanese: 音楽に合わせて一緒に歌う。
cue: Your favourite song comes on during a car journey.
reply: I always sing along to this song in the car.
replyJapanese: 車の中では、いつもこの曲に合わせて歌うんだ。
transferCue: Describe the best moment of a concert.
transferReply: The whole crowd sang along with the band.
transferReplyJapanese: 観客全員が、バンドと一緒に歌いました。
frame: Sing along to something / with someone
nuance: Use to for the music and with for the singer: sing along to the radio, sing along with the band.
nuanceJapanese: 音楽には to、歌い手には with を使う：sing along to the radio、sing along with the band。
contrast: Sing along is only for singing; join in is for any activity that other people are doing.
contrastJapanese: sing along は歌うことだけに使う。join in は、ほかの人がしている活動全般に加わること。

meaning: Use money to buy or pay for something.
japanese: 何かにお金を使う。
cue: You are checking where your money went this month.
reply: I spend too much on coffee every month.
replyJapanese: 毎月、コーヒーにお金を使いすぎています。
transferCue: Ask a friend about a birthday present.
transferReply: How much did you spend on her present?
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女へのプレゼントにいくら使ったの？
nuance: The preposition is on, not for or to. The amount goes between spend and on: spend ten pounds on lunch.
nuanceJapanese: 前置詞は on で、for や to は使わない。金額は spend と on の間に置く：spend ten pounds on lunch。
contrast: Spend on is neutral; waste on means the money brought you nothing useful.
contrastJapanese: spend on は中立的な言い方。waste on は、お金を使っても役に立たなかったという意味。

meaning: Put things back where they are kept after you use them.
japanese: 使った物を元の場所に片づける。
cue: It is bedtime and the floor is covered in toys.
reply: Please tidy away your toys before bed.
replyJapanese: 寝る前に、おもちゃを片づけてね。
transferCue: Get a table ready for a meeting at work.
transferReply: I'll just tidy these papers away before we start.
transferReplyJapanese: 始める前に、この書類を片づけてしまいますね。
nuance: British English; Americans say put away. Separable: tidy away the books or tidy them away.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカでは put away と言う。分離できる：tidy away the books でも tidy them away でもよい。
contrast: Tidy away puts things back in their places; tidy up makes the whole room neat.
contrastJapanese: tidy away は物を元の場所に戻す。tidy up は部屋全体を整える。

meaning: Remove a liquid from a surface with a cloth.
japanese: こぼれた液体を布で拭き取る。
cue: A glass of juice has fallen over on the kitchen floor.
reply: Can you wipe up the juice with this cloth?
replyJapanese: この布で、ジュースを拭き取ってくれる？
transferCue: Say what you did after the cat knocked over its bowl.
transferReply: I wiped the water up before anyone slipped.
transferReplyJapanese: 誰かが滑る前に、水を拭き取りました。
nuance: The object is the liquid, not the surface: wipe up the milk, but wipe the table. Separable: wipe it up.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は液体で、表面ではない：wipe up the milk、ただし wipe the table。分離できる：wipe it up。
contrast: Wipe up removes a spill with a cloth; wipe off removes dirt or marks from a surface.
contrastJapanese: wipe up はこぼれたものを布で拭き取る。wipe off は表面の汚れやしみを拭い去る。

meaning: Most importantly.
japanese: 何よりも。とりわけ。
cue: Give advice to a friend who is learning to drive.
reply: Stay calm, check your mirrors and, above all, take your time.
replyJapanese: 落ち着いて、ミラーを確認して、そして何よりも、あせらないことです。
transferCue: Say what matters most to you in a new flat.
transferReply: Above all, I want somewhere quiet to live.
transferReplyJapanese: 何よりも、静かに暮らせる場所がほしいです。
nuance: It introduces the most important point, often last in a list, and is set off by commas. Do not confuse it with after all, which gives a reason.
nuanceJapanese: いちばん大事な点を示し、列挙の最後に置くことが多い。前後をコンマで区切る。理由を述べる after all と混同しない。

meaning: Before the time when something happens or is needed.
japanese: 前もって。事前に。
cue: A popular restaurant is always full at weekends.
reply: It's best to book ahead of time at weekends.
replyJapanese: 週末は、前もって予約しておくのがいちばんです。
transferCue: Explain why your dinner party was so relaxed.
transferReply: I cooked most of the meal ahead of time, so the evening was easy.
transferReplyJapanese: 料理のほとんどを前もって作っておいたので、当日の夜は楽でした。
nuance: No article: ahead of time, not ahead of the time. It is more common in American English; British speakers often say in advance.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない：ahead of time。ahead of the time とは言わない。アメリカ英語で多く、イギリスでは in advance をよく使う。

meaning: Suddenly and unexpectedly.
japanese: 突然。いきなり。
cue: Tell a friend about a power cut last night.
reply: All at once the lights went out in the whole street.
replyJapanese: 突然、通り全体の明かりが消えました。
transferCue: Describe a change in the weather on your walk home.
transferReply: We were nearly home when all at once it began to snow.
transferReplyJapanese: もうすぐ家というところで、突然雪が降り始めました。
nuance: In this sense it belongs to storytelling and usually starts a clause. It can also mean all at the same time: I can't do everything all at once.
nuanceJapanese: この意味では物語を語るときに使い、ふつう節の頭に置く。「全部いっぺんに」の意味にもなる：I can't do everything all at once。

meaning: Everywhere in or on a place.
japanese: 一面に。至るところに。
cue: The dog ran in from the wet garden.
reply: There were muddy footprints all over the kitchen floor.
replyJapanese: 台所の床じゅうに、泥の足あとが付いていました。
transferCue: Describe the final of a big sports event.
transferReply: People all over the country watched the final.
transferReplyJapanese: 全国の人々が、その決勝戦を見ました。
nuance: A place usually follows: all over the floor, all over the world. On its own after be, it means completely finished: It's all over.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう場所を続ける：all over the floor、all over the world。be 動詞のあとに単独で置くと「すっかり終わった」の意味：It's all over。

meaning: Used at the end of a list to mean and other similar things.
japanese: 〜など。その他いろいろ。
cue: A new colleague asks what you do every day.
reply: I answer emails, book meeting rooms and so on.
replyJapanese: メールの返信や会議室の予約など、いろいろしています。
transferCue: Explain what the corner shop sells.
transferReply: They sell bread, milk, newspapers and so on.
transferReplyJapanese: パン、牛乳、新聞などを売っています。
nuance: It ends a list of two or more examples of the same kind. In writing people often use etc.; and so forth is more formal.
nuanceJapanese: 同じ種類の例を2つ以上挙げたあと、最後に置く。書き言葉では etc. をよく使い、and so forth はより改まった言い方。

meaning: Used to say that the truth is different from what someone thinks.
japanese: 実を言うと。実際のところ。
cue: A colleague thinks you have never been to Scotland.
reply: As a matter of fact, I lived there for two years.
replyJapanese: 実を言うと、2年間そこに住んでいました。
transferCue: Someone is worried that the new meeting day is a problem for you.
transferReply: I don't mind at all. As a matter of fact, I prefer Friday.
transferReplyJapanese: まったく構いません。実のところ、金曜日のほうがいいんです。
nuance: It often corrects what someone has just said, so it can sound sharp if you stress it. Actually is shorter and softer.
nuanceJapanese: 相手の発言を訂正するときによく使うので、強く言うときつく響くことがある。actually のほうが短く、やわらかい。

meaning: Because of something that has just been mentioned.
japanese: その結果。そのために。
cue: Explain why you reached the hotel a day late.
reply: Our flight was cancelled. As a result, we arrived a day late.
replyJapanese: 飛行機が欠航になりました。その結果、到着が1日遅れました。
transferCue: Give a travel update after a night of bad weather.
transferReply: Several roads are closed as a result of the storm.
transferReplyJapanese: 嵐の影響で、いくつかの道路が通行止めになっています。
frame: As a result, … / as a result of something
nuance: At the start of a sentence it takes a comma. Add of before a noun: as a result of the storm. It is fairly formal; in speech people just say so.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭ではコンマを付ける。名詞の前では of を加える：as a result of the storm。やや改まった表現で、会話では so で済ませることが多い。

meaning: Used to say what you think is true when you are not completely sure.
japanese: 私の知るかぎりでは。
cue: A visitor asks whether the manager is free today.
reply: As far as I know, she's in meetings all morning.
replyJapanese: 私の知るかぎりでは、彼女は午前中ずっと会議です。
transferCue: A friend asks whether the pool opens on Sundays.
transferReply: It's still open on Sundays, as far as I know.
transferReplyJapanese: 私の知るかぎりでは、日曜日もまだ開いているよ。
nuance: It shows that you may be wrong, so it is useful when you are not certain. Do not say as long as I know.
nuanceJapanese: 自分が間違っているかもしれないことを示すので、確信がないときに便利。as long as I know とは言わない。

meaning: Used to start talking about a different person or thing.
japanese: 〜はというと。〜については。
cue: Give your honest opinion of a hotel.
reply: The room was lovely, but as for the food, it was poor.
replyJapanese: 部屋は素敵でしたが、食事のほうはというと、いまひとつでした。
transferCue: Tell the waiter what each person wants.
transferReply: The kids want pizza. As for me, I'd like a salad.
transferReplyJapanese: 子どもたちはピザにします。私はというと、サラダをお願いします。
nuance: It moves to a new but related topic, with a comma after the noun. It can sound a little cold about a person: As for him, I don't care.
nuanceJapanese: 関連する別の話題に移るときに使い、名詞のあとにコンマを置く。人について使うと少し冷たく響くことがある：As for him, I don't care。

meaning: Used after a number to say how many are done or taken together.
japanese: 一度に。〜ずつ。
cue: Explain a rule to people waiting for a small lift.
reply: The lift only takes four people at a time.
replyJapanese: このエレベーターは、一度に4人しか乗れません。
transferCue: Describe someone who was late and in a hurry.
transferReply: She ran up the stairs two at a time.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は階段を2段ずつ駆け上がりました。
nuance: It follows a number or amount: one at a time, two at a time. Do not mix it up with at the time, which means then, or at times, which means sometimes.
nuanceJapanese: 数や量のあとに置く：one at a time、two at a time。「当時」の at the time や「ときどき」の at times と混同しない。

meaning: Even when you think about something in the most positive way.
japanese: よく言っても。せいぜい。
cue: A friend asks about a restaurant you did not enjoy.
reply: The food there is average at best.
replyJapanese: あの店の料理は、よく言っても普通です。
transferCue: Give your view of a quick repair at work.
transferReply: At best, it's a short-term answer to the problem.
transferReplyJapanese: それは、よく見ても一時しのぎの解決策です。
nuance: It goes with a weak description and suggests the truth may be worse. No article: at best, not at the best. The opposite is at worst.
nuanceJapanese: 控えめな評価に添えて、実際はもっと悪いかもしれないことを示す。冠詞は付けない：at best。at the best とは言わない。反対は at worst。

meaning: When you see something or someone for the first time.
japanese: 一目見て。一見したところ。
cue: Explain why a small repair took all day.
reply: At first sight the problem looked easy to fix.
replyJapanese: 一見したところ、その問題は簡単に直せそうでした。
transferCue: Tell the story of how your grandparents met.
transferReply: My grandparents fell in love at first sight.
transferReplyJapanese: 祖父母は、一目で恋に落ちました。
nuance: No article before first. It often suggests that a closer look gave a different result. At first glance means the same.
nuanceJapanese: first の前に冠詞は付けない。よく見ると違っていた、という含みになることが多い。at first glance も同じ意味。

meaning: Not more than the amount or number given.
japanese: 多くても。せいぜい。
cue: A friend asks how far the station is from your flat.
reply: It's a ten-minute walk at most.
replyJapanese: 歩いても、せいぜい10分だよ。
transferCue: Tell a customer what a repair is likely to cost.
transferReply: At most, the repair will cost fifty pounds.
transferReplyJapanese: 修理代は、高くても50ポンドです。
nuance: It sets an upper limit and goes before or after the number. At the most means the same. The opposite is at least.
nuanceJapanese: 上限を示し、数の前にもあとにも置ける。at the most も同じ意味。反対は at least。

meaning: In danger of being hurt or harmed.
japanese: 危険にさらされて。
cue: A doctor gives advice during a heatwave.
reply: Older people are most at risk in very hot weather.
replyJapanese: 猛暑のときは、高齢者がもっとも危険にさらされます。
transferCue: Report what happened after days of heavy rain.
transferReply: The floods put several villages at risk.
transferReplyJapanese: 洪水で、いくつかの村が危険にさらされました。
frame: Be at risk / Put someone at risk
nuance: No article: at risk, not at a risk. Add of or from to name the danger: at risk of flooding, at risk from the heat.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない：at risk。at a risk とは言わない。危険の内容は of や from で示す：at risk of flooding、at risk from the heat。

meaning: At the moment in the past when something happened.
japanese: そのときは。当時は。
cue: Look back on a decision you now regret.
reply: Selling the car seemed sensible at the time.
replyJapanese: そのときは、車を売るのが賢明に思えました。
transferCue: Explain why you missed your cousin's wedding.
transferReply: I was living abroad at the time, so I couldn't go.
transferReplyJapanese: 当時は海外に住んでいたので、行けませんでした。
nuance: It points to a past moment already mentioned and often hints that things look different now. At that time is more formal.
nuanceJapanese: すでに話に出た過去の時点を指し、今は見方が違うという含みを持つことが多い。at that time はより改まった言い方。

meaning: Sometimes.
japanese: ときどき。時には。
cue: A friend asks whether you like your new job.
reply: The work is stressful at times, but I enjoy it.
replyJapanese: 仕事はときどきストレスがたまりますが、楽しんでいます。
transferCue: Talk about living far from your family.
transferReply: At times I really miss my family back home.
transferReplyJapanese: 時には、故郷の家族がとても恋しくなります。
nuance: A little more formal than sometimes, and often used about something difficult. Times is plural with no article.
nuanceJapanese: sometimes よりやや改まった言い方で、つらいことについて使うことが多い。times は冠詞なしの複数形。

meaning: Used to say that you are responsible if something goes wrong.
japanese: 自己責任で。自分の責任において。
cue: Warn a friend at a beach with no lifeguard.
reply: There's no lifeguard, so you swim at your own risk.
replyJapanese: 監視員がいないから、泳ぐなら自己責任だよ。
transferCue: Explain the notice on the wall of a station café.
transferReply: Customers leave bags here at their own risk.
transferReplyJapanese: ここに荷物を置く場合は、お客様ご自身の責任となります。
frame: Do something at your own risk
nuance: Common on signs and in warnings: nobody else will pay if something goes wrong. Your changes with the person: at my own risk, at their own risk.
nuanceJapanese: 掲示や警告でよく使い、何かあっても誰も補償しないという意味。your は人に合わせて変わる：at my own risk、at their own risk。

meaning: Moving first in one direction and then back again, many times.
japanese: 行ったり来たり。
cue: Someone was nervous before a job interview.
reply: He walked back and forth outside the room.
replyJapanese: 彼は部屋の外を行ったり来たりしていました。
transferCue: Describe the small ferry in your town.
transferReply: The ferry goes back and forth across the river all day.
transferReplyJapanese: フェリーは一日じゅう、川を行ったり来たりしています。
nuance: The order is fixed: never forth and back. British speakers also say backwards and forwards or to and fro.
nuanceJapanese: 語順は固定で、forth and back とは言わない。イギリスでは backwards and forwards や to and fro とも言う。

meaning: Used to say that something is true although it sounds surprising.
japanese: 信じられないかもしれないが。
cue: Tell a friend something surprising about yourself.
reply: Believe it or not, I've never been on a plane.
replyJapanese: 信じられないかもしれないけど、飛行機に乗ったことが一度もないんだ。
transferCue: Describe your very active uncle.
transferReply: He's seventy and, believe it or not, still plays football every week.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は70歳ですが、信じられないことに、今も毎週サッカーをしています。
nuance: Fixed: it never changes to that or this, and believe stays in the base form. Set it off with commas.
nuanceJapanese: 固定表現で、it を that や this に変えず、believe も原形のまま。コンマで区切って使う。

meaning: Small things or small jobs of different kinds.
japanese: こまごました物。細かい用事。
cue: Tell a colleague why you cannot go to lunch yet.
reply: I've got some bits and pieces to finish first.
replyJapanese: 先に片づけたい細かい用事が、いくつかあるんです。
transferCue: Explain why you are going out for ten minutes.
transferReply: I need a few bits and pieces from the supermarket.
transferReplyJapanese: スーパーで、こまごました物をいくつか買ってきます。
nuance: Informal, and most common in British English; odds and ends means the same. Always plural, and the order never changes.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、イギリス英語でよく使う。odds and ends も同じ意味。常に複数形で、語順は変わらない。
